module_title: Einstein's Equation, Bohr Calculations & Binding Energy (Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate tier transitions into the mathematical rigor of modern physics. It covers Einstein's photoelectric equation, the exact derivation formulas for the Bohr model (radius, velocity, energy), and delves into nuclear physics calculating Mass Defect and radioactive decay parameters.

core_concepts.title: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation
core_concepts.description:
Based strictly on the conservation of energy. The energy of an incident photon ($E$) is utilized in two ways: overcoming the work function ($W$) and imparting maximum kinetic energy ($K_{\text{max}}$) to the ejected electron. $K_{\text{max}} = h\nu - W = hc \left( \frac{1}{\lambda} - \frac{1}{\lambda_0} \right)$.
Stopping Potential ($V_0$): The minimum negative (retarding) potential applied to the anode that stops even the fastest photoelectron. Since $K_{\text{max}} = eV_0$, the equation becomes $eV_0 = h\nu - W$.

core_concepts.title: Mathematical Formulas of Bohr's Model
core_concepts.description:
For the $n$-th orbit of Hydrogen-like atoms ($H, He^+, Li^{2+}$ with atomic number $Z$):
1. Radius: $r_n = 0.529 \frac{n^2}{Z} \text{ \AA}$
2. Orbital Velocity: $v_n = \frac{c}{137} \frac{Z}{n} \approx 2.18 \times 10^6 \frac{Z}{n} \text{ m/s}$
3. Total Energy: $E_n = -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$. (Note the strict relation: Kinetic Energy $K = -E_n$ and Potential Energy $U = 2E_n$).

core_concepts.title: Rydberg Formula
core_concepts.description: When an electron transitions from a higher energy state ($n_2$) to a lower energy state ($n_1$), it emits a photon. The wavelength of this photon is given by: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \left( \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$, where $R_H \approx 1.097 \times 10^7 \text{ m}^{-1}$ is the Rydberg constant.

core_concepts.title: Mass Defect & Binding Energy (BE)
core_concepts.description: The actual resting mass ($M$) of any stable nucleus is always slightly less than the sum of the individual masses of its constituent protons and neutrons. This difference is the Mass Defect ($\Delta m$): $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A-Z) m_n] - M$. By Einstein's mass-energy equivalence ($E=mc^2$), this missing mass was converted into Binding Energy to hold the nucleus together. 1 atomic mass unit (amu) of defect corresponds to exactly $931.5 \text{ MeV}$ of energy.

core_concepts.title: Law of Radioactive Decay
core_concepts.description:
The Rutherford-Soddy law states that the rate of disintegration of a radioactive sample is directly proportional to the number of active nuclei currently present: $\frac{dN}{dt} = -\lambda N$. Integrating this yields the exponential decay equation: $N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$, where $\lambda$ is the decay constant.
Half-Life ($T_{1/2}$): The time required for exactly half of the radioactive nuclei to disintegrate. $T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$.

important_entities.name: Binding Energy per Nucleon (BE/A)
important_entities.key_fact: The ultimate true indicator of a nucleus's stability.
important_entities.significance: Total binding energy does not determine stability; BE per nucleon does. The higher the value of $BE/A$, the more stable the nucleus. Iron ($^{56}\text{Fe}$) has the highest $BE/A$ (approx 8.8 MeV/nucleon), making it the most thermodynamically stable nucleus in the universe.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Stopping Potential vs. Saturation Current Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Understand this dependency completely to secure marks in graphical questions: Stopping potential ($V_0$) depends strictly on the FREQUENCY of incident light (not intensity). Saturation photoelectric current depends strictly on the INTENSITY of incident light (not frequency).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Divide by 2 to the power n
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If exactly $n$ half-lives have elapsed (i.e., total time $t = n \times T_{1/2}$), the number of active radioactive nuclei remaining undecayed can be instantly calculated as $N = N_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n$. The number of decayed nuclei is simply $N_0 - N$.

exam_strategy_tips: If an electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $V$ volts, do not calculate De Broglie wavelength using long momentum formulas. Use the direct shortcut: $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ \AA}$. This saves massive calculation time in JEE/NEET.
